rows.behaviour: A show-wide search's per-episode releases are each judged against their own episode number and title (a release with another episode's title is refused for that reason)
A show-level search passes over single-episode releases (they belong to the season pack / per-episode path) and says why when only episodes were offered
An episode is sized as an episode (episode size band, not the film band)

Season search planning: a fully missing fully aired season is one pack search; a partial or still-airing season, one missing episode, an undated episode, or an episode not yet due keeps it per-episode; different seasons and series are planned independently
A season with a removed (unmonitored) episode is never fetched as a pack; a person asking for a season search still gets packs, automatic searches do not; the inventory names such seasons
A partly installed season pack is judged against exactly the installed episodes (same-plan upgrade only); stale installed evidence refuses
When a season pack is dead or no pack is acceptable, every planned episode is searched instead, honouring each retry window; a failed season dispatch retries only the episodes it covered
Each queued episode search names its show and episode and carries the show so screens can group them

An Usenet job stuck near the end is called downloading, not queued; a percent short of complete is downloading on every client
The strike action's plain-words reason in Activity says why that rule removed the download (each rule has its own sentence)
The notification 'download health remediated' fires only when its toggle is on
A download Deluno did not send (an outside item) is never struck, listed as a problem, or acted on; an old strike for one is cleared on the next pass

rows.behaviour: The processor's callback `POST /api/integrations/processors/events` needs a sign-in (401) and the imports scope (403); a bad status, a completion with no output path, a failed report with no message, more than the maximum number of files, or a too-long path is a 400 saying so and queues nothing; a missing/unknown library is a 400 and a report that matches no hand-off is a 409; a library on standard import refuses completion events (409)

A report repeated for a hand-off already started is accepted again; a late report for an ended hand-off is a 409 ("too late", no import queued); a second completion of a completed hand-off is a 409 saying the hand-off is completed once naming every output; the same completion reported twice imports once

The output must be inside the library's configured clean output folder and about THIS download: an output outside is refused (400) and told on Activity once immediately; a file that is another download's (claimed by another hand-off) is refused and told; a file in the download's own folder, or one that names no download at all, is accepted

The processor's own paths are translated back through the connection's path pairs before anything is compared or imported (most specific pair wins, a disabled pair never matches, no pair = unchanged); a completion reported in the processor's path is imported from Deluno's mapped path

The hand-off is judged by its main video: a partial failure imports what succeeded and reports the count; a small extra the processor left out does not fail a delivered hand-off; a later failed report for one extra does not undo a completed hand-off; a failed main video still fails it; output files without an output path are judged by their main video

A report for an older send of the same path (the release was sent again) is settled there, answered 202 "already handled", and never touches the live send; a first send's late completed report with its output is adopted by the waiting resend and imports once; a report for a send a person removed and re-asked is settled, never a 409; one nobody asked for again is still "too late"
An output already imported (a second copy, a safety-net pass over a cleaned file) is answered "already handled", its copy is deleted, and nothing is blocklisted, removed or searched for

A processor that refuses a file (disposition rejected) -> Deluno refuses and forgets the release, blocklists it and searches again; a release the person chose on search is refused but not searched for; a refusal that cannot be recorded answers "no"; a client that cannot be told yet does not undo the refusal; a held file becomes a recovery case and refuses nothing; a repeat report is answered once

A title the processor keeps refusing (five copies) is not searched for again by the schedule; four are not enough; unblocking a copy lets it resume; a person's own search is theirs to make; an episode is held before any indexer is asked

A report that the download was gone before the processor reached it (failureClass source-gone): Deluno closes it (with a line) when it removed the download itself or the title already has its file, otherwise one plain row with no "Try again" asks only for a new copy; searching for another copy blocklists nothing; dismissing blocklists nothing; a report for an already-completed hand-off changes nothing; judged by the latest send, not the archived one

"Not taken" because another connection owns the file: the first miss waits to be sent again (2, 5 then 10 minutes) and raises nothing; accepted on a retry settles normally; missed every time it becomes one clearable problem naming the shared folder; a removed download stays closed; a hand-off waiting to be sent again is still with the processor so removing the download closes it

Waiting is the processor's to end: a hand-off queued/scheduled/working is waited for however long; the library's limit counts from the last change or the processor answering again; a processor that keeps resetting the clock or says "working" for ever is still given up on in the end; a run scheduled ahead is never a stall; time the processor could not be asked does not count; a processor back after being unreachable gets the whole limit again

At the limit: with no change Deluno imports the original when the library rule says so, otherwise leaves it for a person; a file the processor finished that never arrived ends at the limit; a processor that already started is left to finish; a hand-off the processor never received is "lost" and offers the original; a hand-off just submitted is not called lost; a refused question says to set a webhook secret and gives up on nothing

When a hand-off ends badly the processor's partial output is cleaned: a crashed partial output is deleted, a complete stable output never is, scraps and the now-empty hand-off folder go, a sibling hand-off's folder is never touched

A hand-off whose library was removed, or stopped processing before import, is closed rather than left open for ever; a library whose folder cannot be reached right now keeps its hand-offs; a waiting hand-off whose download was removed raises nothing when the wait runs out, while one whose download is still there is still reported

The processor's output is imported as the grabbed title into the grabbing library (found by name or torrent hash; a folder as what it holds; an episode under its show); a removed film/episode is not imported; a file still being written (temporary name or locked) is not taken until stable; a release refined a second time is imported a second time; the import already queued for this dispatch is not queued again; an output is imported once the processor is done or, with no answer, on the file's own evidence

A film goes end to end through every client on a real install: sent, downloaded, handed to Weir, cleaned, imported, and Activity says "Sent to the download client", "Sent to the processor" and "Imported into the library"

Files in the processor's output that belong to no live hand-off: a leftover of an imported/removed/replaced hand-off is cleared with one Activity line; output a hand-off is still waiting for is never swept; leftovers from an older build are listed for the person; the sweep never reaches outside the output folder; stray video / season folder / scraps are reported on System (a second copy of a held film says so), files being written or queued are never listed
A problem about an output no hand-off will import closes at once everywhere when the resend's hand-off imports that file; the scan does not raise it for a file a live resend will import

What became of the file is told back to the processor: told "imported" (with skipped files and why) or "not imported"; a processor that does not advertise it is told nothing; a refusal does not fail the import; what it said is recorded where a person can read it; an outcome that does not land is said again until it does; a processor that was away is still owed; not told twice; one week then Deluno stops and says so; a conflict is retried hourly for the week; a removed connection leaves nobody to tell; a switched-off processor is not contacted or given up on; a stored outcome keeps only sentenc

Hand-offs that are closed by Deluno itself (a failed hand-off whose film now holds its file, a gone-download row, a failed import) get one plain Activity line each and tell their processor the file was imported once

Transfers/queue reading of a hand-off: a failed hand-off reads as a processing failure with the processor's own reason (attributed to the processor, a client error is not overwritten); a finished processor with no import job yet reads processed; an import that failed or dead-lettered reads import failed; a seeding torrent leaves the processing stage once its refined import completed; a dismissed hand-off is never a problem; a released one follows the ordinary import; a hand-off from a previous fetch is not about this one
A new hand-off, a status change and a new processor state are each pushed live once (no refresh timers)

System > Health reports processor problems: a stalled/lost hand-off with its own reason and options; nothing when none is held; the watched folder the processor reports versus the library's folder (mapped path, per-library folder, ready folder vs downloads folder, no entry = not reported, unknown then ok when it answers again); missing/unmatched output cases

Capabilities: 200 { capabilities[], machine_name, product, version } listing status, cancel, outcome, outcome codes, library folders -> asks and tells accordingly; stores the version
Capabilities: 401 { detail } (no secret sent) -> status: hand-offs are not judged and the connection shows "refused the webhook secret"; outcome: stays owed
Capabilities: 401 { detail } (wrong secret) -> status: Activity processing.status-forbidden, connection "degraded", hand-off kept; outcome: processing.outcome-delayed, owed, no outcome post sent
Capabilities: connection refused -> hand-off kept, silence noted on the hand-off; outcome owed

Library folders: 200 { libraries[]: id, name, media_type, watched_folder, work_folder, output_folder, manager_library_key, folders_from_manager, minimum_file_size_bytes } -> checks each library's folders against Weir's; a hand-off leaves out files under the minimum size
Hand-off: 200 { status: "ok", source, event, media_scope, enqueued } for a file -> hand-off recorded as submitted
Hand-off: 200 for a file not in the watched folder yet -> same; Weir's status then says what it found
Hand-off: 200 for a release folder -> same
Hand-off: 200 for a release folder with sourceFiles -> same
Hand-off: 200 for the same source sent again -> same; the older send's own report is settled apart (section 7)
Hand-off: 200 { status: "ignored", source } (no source path in the body) -> recorded as submitted. Deluno never sends a body without a source path, which the request test pins
Hand-off: 400 { detail } (no workflow watches the folder) -> hand-off marked failed with "The processor refused the hand-off with HTTP 400: <Weir's words>"
Hand-off: 401 { detail } (wrong secret) -> same, HTTP 401
Hand-off: connection refused -> "Could not submit the hand-off. Check the processor connection"; sent again by the planner
Status: 200 queued with queuePosition (12, 6) -> stored on the hand-off and shown as the place in line; waits; no Activity line
Status: 200 working, message "Weir has claimed this file and is checking it now." -> stored and shown; waits; no stall until the library's limit
Status: 200 completed with outputPath and outputFiles -> stored and shown; waits for Weir's report or the output folder to bring the file in; never ended on the status alone

Status: 200 completed, outputPath null (Weir had cleaned the file for an older send) -> stored; for a hand-off that replaced an earlier send Deluno matches the cleaned file it finds at once and queues the import (processing.completed.import-queued); otherwise waits

Status: 200 failed, message (file under the minimum size) -> hand-off ends failed with "Weir reports failed for <release>: <Weir's message>"; Activity processing.failed; a case to clear is raised (processor-failed)
Status: 200 cancelled -> hand-off ends stopped, "Weir stopped work on <release>."; Activity processing.cancelled

Status: 404 { detail: "Weir has never received this hand-off." } -> inside 15 minutes of the last change: nothing (not believed). After: hand-off ends lost, Activity processing.lost, case processor-lost raised
Status: status of a hand-off read after a refused cancel -> as above
Status: 200 completed: a single-file source (qBittorrent) -> as above. **outputPath is flat in the output folder (<output>\<file>.mkv), no folder named after the source** (#1262)

Status: 200 completed: a release folder (Transmission) and a Usenet job (SABnzbd; Deluno names the file inside the job folder) -> as above; the output keeps the folder: <output>\<release>\<release>.mkv
Status: 200 queued, polled every minute while Weir is paused -> waits
Status: 401 { detail: "Invalid or missing X-Webhook-Secret header." } (wrong secret, or none) -> as for the capabilities refusal
Status: 404 { detail } for an unknown or malformed id -> as no-record
Status: 404 { detail: "Unknown media manager source 'x'." }, checked before the secret -> none
Status: 403 { detail: "Set a webhook secret in Weir so a media manager can ask about hand-offs." } (no connection of that source has a secret) -> as the 401
Status: connection refused -> hand-off kept; the observation records when Weir went quiet; never counted against the file
Cancel: 204 (still queued) -> hand-off ends stopped, "...and it was asked to drop <release>"; Activity processing.cancelled

Cancel: 409 { detail: "This hand-off is working, so Weir did not cancel it." } -> nothing changed; "Weir has started work ... Deluno will not interrupt it" (a removed title ends it anyway and its output is not imported)
Cancel: 409 { detail: "...is completed, so Weir did not cancel it." } -> same: nothing changed; the next status poll shows completed
Cancel: 204 as Deluno sent it: "Stop waiting" on a hand-off Weir holds queued -> as the row above
Cancel: 401 (wrong secret) -> nothing changed; the hand-off is not ended as dropped
Cancel: 404 { detail } (an id Weir never received) -> hand-off ends stopped, as if it were dropped
Cancel: 409 { detail: "This hand-off is completed, so Weir did not cancel it." } (a hand-off finished long ago) -> nothing changed

Cancel: 403 { detail: "Missing X-Requested-With header…" } (an Origin header with no X-Requested-With on a POST or DELETE; Deluno sends no Origin) -> not sent by Deluno; recorded so Weir's rule stays known
Cancel: connection refused -> hand-off ends stopped and says "it could not be told, so it may still have <release>"
Outcome: 200 { handoffId, outcome, released: true, message } -> delivered, one attempt; processing.outcome-reported "... It released its copy."; never asked again
Outcome: 200 released: false (Weir's copy is the library file) -> delivered; Activity says Deluno told Weir it has the file and repeats Weir's own words
Outcome: 200, imported with a reason note -> delivered; Activity carries the note in brackets
Outcome: 200, not-imported, no reason / the default words / an import refusal -> delivered; Activity "Deluno told Weir it will not import <release>: <reason>"; Weir kept its copy

Outcome: 409 { detail, code: "handoff_not_finished" } (queued, working) -> stays owed: pending, next attempt a minute later, then doubling to an hour; Activity processing.outcome-delayed said once; gives up after a week
Outcome: 409 { detail, code: "handoff_ended" } (cancelled, failed) -> refused, one attempt, never asked again; Activity processing.outcome-not-reported with Weir's words
Outcome: 409 { detail, code: "outcome_already_recorded" } -> settled, never asked again; Activity processing.outcome-kept "kept its earlier answer"
Outcome: 404 { detail } -> "never received", not a failure, never asked again; Activity processing.outcome-never-received
Outcome: 401 (wrong secret) -> stays owed; the connection is shown refused
Outcome: 404 { detail: "Weir has never received this hand-off." } -> as the row above

Outcome: 422 (unknown outcome word, missing outcome, a body that is not JSON; checked before the secret) and 415 (not declared JSON) { detail: [...] } -> the report was wrong; never sent again (Deluno never sends such a body)
Outcome: connection refused -> stays owed with "Deluno could not reach Weir."; processing.outcome-delayed
Reports Weir sends to Deluno: completed with outputPath and outputFiles (a single file; a release folder; a Usenet job) -> an import is queued
Reports Weir sends to Deluno: completed for a release that was sent again -> the newer send settles from its own report
Reports Weir sends to Deluno: completed after the person stopped waiting (the hand-off ended dismissed) -> no import is queued
Reports Weir sends to Deluno: failed, file under the minimum size (disposition: "held") -> nothing imported; the hand-off ends failed
Reports Weir sends to Deluno: failed with failureClass: "source_gone" (the download was deleted) -> the hand-off ends as source gone
Reports Weir sends to Deluno: failed, a file Weir cannot read (disposition: "held") -> nothing imported

Status (Weir 1.0.0-rc.18): 200 rejected (an audio-only file under Weir's reject policy) is read by its word with Weir's message -> the hand-off ends failed "Weir reports rejected for <release>: <Weir's message>", Activity processing.failed, a case to clear

Status (Weir 1.0.0-rc.18): a single file sent again while Weir held the first -> the first send is cancelled ("This release was sent again ...") and ends stopped, the second works and completes WITH its output path; both shapes of a resend's finished status (with and without a path) are read

Status (Weir 1.0.0-rc.18): a different file sent under a name the output already holds -> "replace" completes on the same output path, "keep both" completes as stem (2).ext beside the first; either is found as the same download's
Status (Weir 1.0.0-rc.18): a season-pack folder works then completes with the folder as outputPath; a pack with one unreadable episode waits queued (the settle-time message) then works
Outcome: 409 handoff_not_finished (the plain recording, without the queued or working suffix) is read by its code as busy and owed again in a minute
Reports Weir sends to Deluno (rc.18): failed with failureClass "superseded" (the older of two sends) -> accepted, the older hand-off ends failed; with no row it is a 409

Reports Weir sends to Deluno (rc.18): completed for the send that took over a resend, and for two files under one name (replace: the same path; keep both: stem (2).ext) -> accepted, one import from the path named; with no row a 409

Reports Weir sends to Deluno (rc.18): completed for a season-pack folder of two episodes -> one import of the folder; failed (held) with the two good episodes of three in outputFiles -> what succeeded is imported and the hand-off fails with the count

Reports Weir sends to Deluno (rc.18): failed, disposition rejected, failureClass preflight -> with the download in a client: accepted, release blocked and removed by Deluno; without it: 409 "could not refuse that release" and the hand-off is kept for a person
Reports Weir sends to Deluno (rc.18): a finished report answered 503, 401 or 403 once is not sent again within 300 s (503) or 130 s (401, 403); sent again, a report imports once
Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: 200 [] on a Deluno with no hand-off, for every library and for one -> reply-handoffs-empty

Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: 200 a list of hand-offs (id, libraryId, mediaType, clientId, queueItemId, releaseName, sourcePath, processorName, status, outputPath, importJobId, failureMessage, createdUtc, updatedUtc, processor, outcome, processorConnectionId, sourceFiles), newest change first, filtered by libraryId, limited by take -> reply-handoffs-listed

Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: 200 hand-offs carrying outcome in each delivery state (pending, delivered, refused, given-up, never-received, settled, replaced) -> reply-handoffs-with-outcomes

Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: 200 { libraries: [] }, and 404 { error: "library_not_found", message: "Deluno has no library with the id <id>." } for a libraryId Deluno does not have (a 404 with no body means only that the route is missing, #1267) -> reply-download-destinations-empty

Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: 200 { libraries[]: libraryId, libraryName, mediaType, downloadsPath, processorOutputPath, importWorkflow, destinations[], processorConnection }, with the processor connection and its pathMappings for a library that hands to a processor, null for one that does not; 404 { error: "library_not_found", message } for an unknown library -> reply-download-destinations-libraries

Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: 202 with the hand-off as it now stands (status released) and a location of the library's hand-off list, for a hand-off that is failed, timed-out, stalled, lost or cancelled -> reply-import-original-accepted

Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: 409 { message } ("The original can only be imported once the processor has stopped working on it...") for waiting, submitted, accepted, started, completed, rejected, released and dismissed -> reply-import-original-not-yet

Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: 404 { error: "handoff_not_found", message: "Deluno has no hand-off with the id <id>." } for a hand-off Deluno has no record of -> reply-import-original-unknown

Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: 404 { error: "nothing_recorded", message } ("Deluno has nothing recorded to tell the processor...") for a hand-off with no outcome recorded, and for an unknown one -> reply-send-again-nothing-recorded
Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: 200 { message, outcome }, the outcome given up because the processor connection was removed -> reply-send-again-connection-removed
Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: 200 { message, outcome }, Weir acknowledged it and kept its copy (Weir 200, released: false) -> reply-send-again-delivered
Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: 200 { message, outcome }, Weir acknowledged it and let go of its copy (Weir 200, released: true) -> reply-send-again-delivered-released
Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: 200, Weir says it holds an answer (Weir 409 outcome_already_recorded): settled -> reply-send-again-weir-has-its-answer
Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: 200, Weir says the hand-off ended (Weir 409 handoff_ended): refused for good -> reply-send-again-weir-hand-off-ended
Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: 200, Weir has not finished (Weir 409 handoff_not_finished): still owed, nextAttemptUtc set -> reply-send-again-weir-not-finished
Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: 200, Weir never received the hand-off (Weir 404): never-received -> reply-send-again-weir-never-received
Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: 200, Weir refuses the secret (Weir 401 on its capabilities): still owed -> reply-send-again-weir-refuses-secret
Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: 200, Weir cannot be reached: still owed -> reply-send-again-weir-unreachable
Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: 401 (no body) on each of the four routes, with no credential -> reply-no-sign-in

Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: a key with only the read scope: 403 { message } on the two reads (the route's own scope check, "This API key does not include the required scope: imports.") and 403 { error, required, granted } on the two writes (the authorization policy) -> reply-key-without-imports-scope

Deluno's replies to the calls Weir makes: a key with only the imports scope: the two reads answer 200 and the two writes pass the scope check (404 for an unknown id) -> reply-key-with-imports-scope-only

Every API route found from the endpoint map answers 401 to a request with no credential; only the nine public routes (sign-in, first account, bootstrap status, calendar feed, Seerr webhook, artwork, three health probes) answer without one, each listed with its reason, and a route added later is walked without a new test

Every API route answers 401 to a wrong API key (in X-Api-Key or as the bearer), a made-up session token (in the header or the address), a session whose user is gone, a session signed out since (stale security stamp) and an expired session
Every API route answers 403 to a valid key that holds every scope except the one the route needs, and no route may ask for a signed-in caller only (each names a scope policy)

A request with no credential is answered 401 before the route looks at its body or content type: a body that is not JSON, plain text, no content type and no body all get 401, never a 400 or 415 that would tell a stranger about the route
Every route that takes a JSON body, found from the endpoint map, answers a missing body and a body whose members all have the wrong type with a 4xx, never a 5xx and never an unhandled exception

A request body over its route's limit is refused 413 with a plain "too large" message on every route that takes a JSON body, before the route runs; each route has the limit that fits what it takes (256 KB by default, 1 MB for an import preview, 5 MB for a subtitle upload, 256 MB for a backup restore)

A saved text member over its length limit (a name over 200 characters, a description or notes over 4,000, a path over 4,096, a URL over 2,048, a pattern over 2,000, a key over 1,000) is refused 400 with a plain message naming the member and the most allowed, without echoing the text; a name at exactly its limit is saved; members that hold a whole document are bounded by the body limit alone

A missing, malformed or wrongly typed JSON body is answered with a plain message, in the message member the web app and the SDK read first, naming the member at fault and carrying no framework wording (no type names, line numbers or JSON paths), on every route that takes a body, including the routes that read their body by hand
A folder or file path with a null character, or longer than 4,096 characters, sent to the scan-folder and file-changed routes is refused 400, never a 500
POST /api/filesystem/import/execute-batch with no list of files is refused 400 with a reason that says a list of files is needed

One shared rule decides whether a path that came from outside stays inside its folder: dots, repeats and mixed separators are removed, a path that climbs above its start cannot be normalised, a path is inside a root only when it lands below it (a sibling folder sharing the name prefix is not), a part that climbs out or is rooted is refused with one plain reason, and the file-changed route takes only a full path without dot segments

A client path or a processor path that climbs out with .. is refused with a plain reason when it is mapped, in both directions for a processor, and never leaves the target root; dots that stay inside are tidied and clean paths are left alone
A processor source path that climbs out with .. gives no output paths to look in, so the clean-output sweep never reaches outside the processor output folder
The recycle bin will not take a path that climbs out of the library with ..: nothing is stored and the file outside the library is left where it is

Deleting a download client's files refuses a path that climbs out with .. even when it resolves to something real: the same folder by its plain path is deletable, but by the climbing path nothing is removed and no leftovers are cleared
A path a download client reports is kept (trimmed) only when it does not climb out with . or .. segments; a clean path with two dots inside a name (Movie..2020) is kept; blank is nothing

qBittorrent: the content path or save path it reports is read as it is when it is clean, and never used as the source path of the queue, an import or a delete when it climbs out with ..; the recorded real reply is replayed with the one value swapped for a climbing path

Transmission: the download folder, or a torrent named .. it reports is read as it is when it is clean, and never used as the source path of the queue, an import or a delete when it climbs out with ..; the recorded real reply is replayed with the one value swapped for a climbing path

Deluge: the save path it reports is read as it is when it is clean, and never used as the source path of the queue, an import or a delete when it climbs out with ..; the recorded real reply is replayed with the one value swapped for a climbing path

SABnzbd: the finished job's storage it reports is read as it is when it is clean, and never used as the source path of the queue, an import or a delete when it climbs out with ..; the recorded real reply is replayed with the one value swapped for a climbing path

NZBGet: the job folder (DestDir) it reports is read as it is when it is clean, and never used as the source path of the queue, an import or a delete when it climbs out with ..; the recorded real reply is replayed with the one value swapped for a climbing path
uTorrent: the save path it reports is never used as the source path when it climbs out with ..; clean paths are read as they are (no recording of uTorrent exists yet, so the reply is hand-built)

A folder or file name Deluno renders is at most 255 bytes whatever the title (long, two-byte, CJK or emoji), cut by bytes and never through a surrogate pair, keeping the year and the file extension and cut per path segment; a name that was already fine renders exactly as before

A rendered name never ends in a dot or a space (Windows drops them), keeps a dot inside a name and trims only the end of the whole name, never comes out empty when the title is only dots and spaces, and holds no control character or line break
The title and year Deluno renders into a folder name read back as the same title and year (including the year 2100), a template with no tokens renders as itself and an unknown token stays visible

Every parser reads an episode marker, a daily date and a year the same way: S01E01E02E03, E05-E07, 10-12 and 3x04 with any separator; a daily date in full with any separator and never a date off the calendar; a year from 1900 to 2199 and never a resolution (2160p) as a year; a version suffix or a separated tag (v2, REPACK, PROPER) after the marker still reads that episode, and anything else glued on does not; the same for an absolute number and the feed reader

A release name for an episode is accepted for exactly the season and episode it carries and refused for any other, whether it is joined with dots, spaces, dashes or underscores, written S01E01E02, NxNN or as a range, a season pack, an absolute number or a daily date, in any case and with a one-digit season

A tracker release with neither a download link nor a magnet is skipped and logged once, and the rest of the page is kept; a title with a control character or a backspace still gives a feed that can be written

A release written as a feed reads back with its title, size and publish date as the same values, the date as the same UTC instant and the size never negative; a date or title of any text never throws and a feed body of any text gives no releases rather than an error

Every screen reads a size through one formatter: a count just under a unit boundary reads in the next unit (1,048,575 bytes is 1 MB, not 1024 KB), a fraction of a byte keeps its unit, zero is 0 B, and a missing, negative or non-finite size reads a dash, never NaN, undefined or Infinity; larger sizes never read as smaller

is monotonic: a larger size never reads as a smaller amount (whole bytes)
is within rounding of the real size, so the unit is correct
never shows a value of 1024 or more in a unit that has a larger one (just under a unit boundary) - DEFECT: 1048575 reads 1024 KB
DEFECT (shrunk case): a size just under 1 MB reads 1024 KB, not 1 MB

a subnormal size reads 0 B, not Infinity

rows.behaviour: NZBGet paused by its own reload over an invalid line in its settings (its log says "Invalid option" and "Pausing all activities due to errors in configuration"): Deluno shows the client paused, and once the line is fixed and NZBGet reloaded it is not shown paused; the log is read only when the status says downloads are paused

A NZBGet pause over errors in its settings is said in plain words on the client's health and counted as a client warning that can be cleared from the Connections screen; a pause the person chose is not an error, an old error followed by a clean start reads as an ordinary pause, the warning goes once the errors are fixed, and clearing the warning resumes NZBGet

Every settings write Deluno makes to a download client sends only the keys it means to change and every key is a real setting of that app, checked against the app's recorded reply: SABnzbd's provider write sends only the server keys, qBittorrent's content blocklist sends only the excluded file names

The setup Deluno runs on a client it installed writes through the client's own settings call and sends only the keys it means to change: qBittorrent the folder and automatic-management keys, Transmission the three folder keys, Deluge the three folder keys, SABnzbd the two folder settings and the category name and folder; running the NZBGet setup twice saves the same list the second time with no runtime-only values

Weir's plain-text "Internal Server Error" (the only 5xx it can give, for an exception nothing handled) on a status poll, a cancel or an outcome report is "not now": the status is asked again, the hand-off is not given up on, the outcome stays owed and is sent again (the reply is built in the test: Weir cannot be made to give it on purpose)

A 503 (database busy) from Weir on any call (capabilities, hand-off, status, cancel, outcome) stays retryable and carries the time Weir asked in Retry-After (seconds or a date, cut to an hour, plus at most a tenth); Deluno sends nothing more to Weir until that time has passed, a reply with no Retry-After holds nothing back, a JSON 500 is retryable like the plain-text one and asks for no wait, and an outcome report is owed again after the time asked and not after the usual minutes (the 503 and the JSON 500 are Weir 1.0.0-rc.18's own recorded replies, `database-busy-outcome` and `internal-error-outcome`, with only the Retry-After value changed where a test is about another one)

A processor's finished hand-off that names no output path is still found where the processor puts the cleaned file: a single file at the watched root lands flat in the output folder, a film in a release folder keeps that folder, a name collision that renamed only the file is found, another file beside it is never taken for it, nothing outside the processor's own output folder is matched, and the watched folder comes from the processor's own list through the path mapping

Through the watcher, a hand-off Weir answers "completed" with no output path queues the import of the flat file in the output folder: at once for a hand-off that replaced an earlier send, and once it has waited for one that replaced nothing; nothing is queued when the folder holds only another file

The output sweep clears what a finished-with hand-off left in the places Weir puts it, a release folder holding a file that was sent and a flat file renamed for a name collision, leaves an unrelated file alone, and keeps the release folder of a hand-off still with the processor

The picker installs the newest release that has the installer, its checksum file and a checksum line for the installer, skipping a newer release published before its files were uploaded, an installer that answers 404 after its checksum arrived and a checksum file that does not list the installer; the install log names the release used and why the newer one was skipped, the walk stays within six calls, and every release without files gives one plain message; a rate limit keeps its own message

rTorrent: the download folder it lists is dropped when it climbs out with .., and a delete with data never deletes a base path that climbs out even when it resolves to a real folder (d.erase is still sent and the message says its files could not be safely found); no recording of rTorrent exists yet, so the reply is hand-built with the one value swapped

A backup archive entry that climbs out of the data folder with .. (in any spelling, with forward or back slashes) is skipped and nothing is written outside the data folder, while a clean entry in the same archive is restored

An import whose source path has .. in it is refused and never imported, copied, moved or deleted from, though the file it reaches is real and inside the downloads folder once resolved: the file stays, no title is added and nothing lands in the library
The processor output root counts as within itself, as does a file below it, but a sibling folder that only shares the root's text and a path that climbs out of it do not

Cleaning up an abandoned hand-off never touches a hand-off folder name that climbs out of the processor output root with .. or names the output root itself: a file beside the root and a file in the root stay

POST /api/integrations/external/file-changed refuses a path that has .. or a dot segment in it (with forward or back slashes), a relative path and a path ending in a dot segment with a 400 that gives the one plain reason, before the disk or the library is touched, though the file it reaches exists

POST /api/custom-formats/import refuses a body that is not one format (an object) or a list of them (a number, a piece of text, true, null) with a 400 and a message that says a JSON object is expected, instead of answering an error per item

rows.behaviour: Movies and TV shows libraries on the real server: the empty library says so in words, the add dialog sends the title and year, search narrows through a real request and says when nothing matches, a row Search now and Refresh metadata send their requests and say what happened, and Remove asks first then removes

proofs.name: an empty ${variant.name} library says so in words and offers to add the first title
the add dialog sends the title and year the person typed, and the new ${variant.name} title appears
search narrows ${variant.name} through a real request, and a search that matches nothing says so
a row's Search now sends one real search for that title, and Refresh metadata one refresh, each saying what it did
selecting a title and choosing Remove asks first, sends one remove request, and the title is gone from the server

rows.behaviour: Activity on the real server: the recorded history lists with a sentence, status and time; a row opens its event drawer and Close shuts it; the In progress, Failed and Needs a decision chips narrow the list and say so in words when empty

proofs.name: Everything lists what Deluno recorded, with a plain sentence, a status and a time on each row
a row opens its event in a drawer that says what happened, and Close shuts it
the ${chip} chip narrows the list and, with nothing there, says so in words

rows.behaviour: Transfers on the real server with nothing downloading: it says so in words, shows every counter and the safeguards as Off, and Manual import previews a real file through the server without writing anything

proofs.name: with nothing sent to a download client the screen says so in words and every counter is there
the cleanup safeguards read Off on a fresh install, as nothing is automatic until chosen
Manual import opens a drawer, offers one file or a folder, and a real file previews through the server

rows.behaviour: System Backups and Recycle bin on the real server: counts and wording match the server, Create backup, the schedule, a real archive previewing as valid and a non-backup refused in words, and the empty recycle bin with its cleanup preview and retention settings

proofs.name: the screen's count and wording match what the server holds
Create backup sends one request, the server then holds the backup and the screen lists it with a download
the automatic schedule saves what was chosen, and the server keeps it
a real backup archive previews as valid, and a file that is not a backup is refused in words
an empty recycle bin says so in words, and the server agrees
Clean expired items asks the server what it would take, says so in words, and removes nothing
the retention settings save what was typed and the server keeps it
